ganglioside GM1 promotes long term survival and prevents DNA fragmentation in PC12 cells deprived of NGF.

ganglioside GM1 promotes the survival of PC 12 and sympathetic neurons in serum- and NGF-free conditions, and prevents DNA fragmentation in serum-free PC 1 cells, an indicator of apoptotic neuronal death.
ganglioside GM1 promotes the survival of neuronal cells deprived from growth factors.

the role of glycolipid in the survival of neurons in culture.
the molecular basis of neurodegeneration.
the mechanisms by which GM1 protects neurons from death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gangliosides are neurotrophic factors.
ganglioside GM1 is a potent neuroprotective agent that can prevent the death of neuronal cells deprived either of trophic factor support or of other survival factors.

the GM1 gangliosides have been shown to be effective in the prevention of neuronal cell death in vitro, and that they may have therapeutic potential in the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ganglioside GM1 protects neurons from death after withdrawal of neurotrophic support.
ganglioside GM1 promotes neuronal cell survival by a mechanism that is independent of NGF.
ganglioside GM1 promotes survival of neuronal cells deprived either of trophic factors or excitotoxic agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ganglioside GM1 promotes survival of neuronal cells deprived from neurotrophic factor, and that this effect is independent of the protein kinase C pathway.
